title: Too Many Bots in the Kitchen? Williams Sonoma Bans AI Shoppers
key_facts: Williams Sonoma and Pottery Barn emailed customers this week with updated terms of service barring customer AI agents from shopping on their websites without the company's written permission (KQED).

The terms apply to all brands under parent Williams-Sonoma Inc. and forbid letting any "agent", "assistant", bot or AI-enabled software use accounts or buy on a customer's behalf; automated tools must identify themselves.
The company can block any third party "including where you have purported to authorize such access", and customers stay responsible for all activity on their accounts.
Williams-Sonoma Inc. did not respond to KQED's request for comment in time for publication.

In August a federal appeals court ruled in Amazon's lawsuit against Perplexity that the user, not the AI company, is the one accessing a website when an agent shops, but said companies can still set rules through terms of service.
Law professor Lauren Willis of Loyola Marymount University says the terms are likely legal for now and wants the law to require retailers to accept shoppers' agents.

Eric Goldman, associate dean for research and professor at Santa Clara University School of Law, says blocking often looks like an overreaction to AI and expects retailers eventually to lose the ability to single out AI agents.
